I also need to make sure the expected output format is followed exactly and I am careful about the aliases provided.

Simple enough. I started with the core question: “Which athlete carried the Olympic flame during the 2024 Summer Olympics opening ceremony?” Then, I created surface questions. For surface questions, I aimed for variations on phrasing, trying to be natural and not leak any information from the answer.

Next, I handled the neighbor card: *Simone Biles received the Olympic flag during the handover at the 2024 Summer Olympics closing ceremony.* The given alias for this one, "2024 Summer Olympics closing ceremony" is a clear mistake. Rule 7 specifically says to avoid topic aliases and instead utilize only valid answer aliases, I will use "Biles". The core question is: "Which athlete received the Olympic flag during the handover at the 2024 Summer Olympics closing ceremony?" For the surface questions, I was similarly careful about not including anything not in the fact itself. Again, I focused on varied phrasing and natural language. I am careful to only use terms present in the fact, and I avoid the mention of anything not clearly defined in the fact.

Now, with both cards processed, I reviewed the questions I generated. I made adjustments for better flow. I had to ensure each set of questions had one core and three surface questions. They need to be answer-aware and completely avoid leaking any information about the answer. All of the surface questions and core question follow these constraints.
